N5.M1: Read and write all hiragana and katakana, recognize vowel sounds and sound contrasts, and greet and introduce yourself politely.
N5.M2: Build correct simple sentences about routines, locations, and possession, and understand the Japanese particle system.
N5.M3: Describe people and things with i/na-adjectives, express existence and location, count objects, and handle prices.
N5.M4: Talk about yesterday and last week by mastering the past tense of verbs, adjectives, and the copula.
N5.M5: Master the te-form — the most productive N5 pattern — for linking actions, requesting, asking permission, and ongoing activities.
N5.M6: Express reasons, contrast, comparisons of two or more things, and degree — patterns that turn simple sentences into connected speech.
N5.M7: Express wants, likes/dislikes, and ability, and master the dictionary form that underpins advanced patterns.
N5.M8: Handle rules and obligations, future plans, frequency, and the ta-form (plain past) for key N5 patterns.
N5.M9: Turn knowledge into exam performance: speed-reading for information, eliminating distractors, and keeping listening stamina.
N5.M10: Take a full N5 simulation in Real mode, analyze mistakes by category, and close gaps before the real exam.

N4.n4-m1: Talk about ability with the potential form, link reasons with 〜し, do two things at once with 〜ながら, and consolidate 〜たり〜たりする.
N4.n4-m2: Handle giving–receiving actions (〜てあげる/くれる/もらう) and understand keigo: sonkeigo vs. kenjougo concepts, basic patterns, and the most common special verbs.
N4.n4-m3: Express intention with the volitional form and master the four conditionals (と/〜たら/〜ば/〜ても) with their nuances.
N4.n4-m4: Give advice (〜たほうがいい), distinguish preparation–state–accident (〜ておく/〜てある/〜てしまう), and express purpose and change of ability.
N4.n4-m5: Understand and use the passive (including the suffering passive and formal passive) as well as the causative and causative-passive in news and daily contexts.
N4.n4-m6: Use keigo correctly in real situations: taking/placing phone calls, writing simple business emails, and interacting at work.
N4.n4-m7: Express conjecture and impression with the right nuance: the two 〜そうだ, 〜みたい/〜らしい/〜ようだ, 〜はずだ, and 〜べきだ.
N4.n4-m8: Express degree (〜すぎる, 〜やすい/〜にくい), movement relative to the speaker (〜てくる/〜ていく), and precise time aspects (〜ところ, 〜たばかり, 〜ばかり, 〜うちに).
N4.n4-m9: Turn knowledge into exam performance at N4 difficulty: skimming mid-length texts, eliminating distractors, and surviving a full single-play listening section.
N4.n4-m10: Take a complete N4 mock in Real mode, review mistakes by category, and close remaining gaps before the real exam.

N3.n3-m1: Automate the most error-prone N4 patterns (suffering passive, causative-passive, 〜ことにする/〜ことになる, 〜うちに) and master N3 transition patterns: 〜させていただく, hard conditions (〜てからでないと/〜ないことには), and cause-effect markers (〜ものだから/〜ことだから, 〜おかげで/〜せいで).
N3.n3-m2: Enter formal written Japanese: read and write である style, use logical conjunctions, and express formal relations between concepts (〜に対して, 〜に関して).
N3.n3-m3: Express resolve and effort (volitional + とする, 〜ようとする, 〜まい), conditional possibility (〜ものなら), and compulsion/irresistibility (〜ざるを得ない, 〜ないではいられない, 〜てはいられない, 〜てたまらない/〜てしかたがない, 〜得る, 〜かねる).
N3.n3-m4: Master formal conditionals and concession: 〜としたら/〜とすれば, the 〜にしても/〜にせよ/〜といっても/〜とはいえ family, and conditional-resolve markers (〜からには, 〜以上は, 〜上は, 〜次第).
N3.n3-m5: Express impression and degree precisely: suffixes 〜っぽい/〜がち/〜気味/〜げ, 〜ぶる/〜めく, 〜だらけ/〜まみれ/〜ずくめ, conclusion markers 〜わけだ/〜わけではない/〜わけがない, 〜ものだ/〜ことだ, and onomatopoeia (giongo/gitaigo) in narration.
N3.n3-m6: Master precise time expressions (〜以来, 〜最中に, 〜ついでに, 〜がてら/〜かたわら, 〜や否や/〜が早いか/〜なり, 〜向け/〜向き) and advanced business keigo for emails, documents, and formal work situations.
N3.n3-m7: Read 短文 and 中文 with strategy: gradual change (〜につれて/〜にしたがって/〜とともに), contrast (〜一方だ/〜一方で), ongoing aspect (〜つつある), and compound verbs (〜きる/〜ぬく/〜通す/〜かける).
N3.n3-m8: Conquer 長文, 情報検索, and opinion texts, plus full-speed listening: coverage (〜をめぐって/〜にわたって/〜を通じて/〜に伴って), document formality (〜を機に/〜を皮切りに/〜にかけては/〜に際して/〜を限りに/〜をもって), and simile style (〜んばかりに/〜とばかりに/〜かのようだ).
N3.n3-m9: Turn knowledge into exam performance at N3 difficulty: skimming long texts, eliminating nuanced distractors, and surviving a full-speed single-play listening section.
N3.n3-m10: Take a complete N3 mock in Real mode, review mistakes by category and strand, and close remaining gaps before the real exam.

N2.n2-m1: Consolidate foundational N3 patterns (〜ざるを得ない, 〜わけだ, 〜ものだ) and master N2 limitation/essence expressions (〜にほかならない, 〜にすぎない, 〜に足る/〜に堪える, 〜甲斐がある), while forcing である-style production in every piece of writing.
N2.n2-m2: Master N2-level conjecture (〜おそれがある, 〜かねない, 〜に相違ない, 〜ほかない) and rhetorical denial (〜ものか), and consolidate the 〜っぽい/〜がち/〜気味 family from N3 at written-text depth.
N2.n2-m3: Master formal concession and conditions (〜にしろ/〜にせよ/〜であれ, 〜いかんにかかわらず/〜を問わず, 〜からして/〜からすると) — the core toolkit of N2 argumentation — with an N3 conditional review.
N2.n2-m4: Master irrepressible emotion (〜を禁じ得ない, 〜てやまない, 〜ずにはおかない) and as-if emphasis (〜んばかり/〜とばかり) — the patterns most often used as N2 distractors.
N2.n2-m5: Master manner/state expressions (〜なり〜なり, 〜かたわら, 〜そばから, 〜つつある) and appearance/impression (〜ざま, 〜ぶり, 〜じみる, 〜ともなく) — the grammar vocabulary that separates N2 from N3.
N2.n2-m6: Master formal written keigo: 謙譲語II (ご〜いただく, お〜申し上げる, 拝〜), document formulas (謹啓・敬具・記・以上), and complete business emails — as a life skill and exam material.
N2.n2-m7: Read newspaper Japanese: headline passives, news expressions (〜模様だ, 〜とのことだ, 〜ものとみられる), and party/source markers — the foundation for 長文 and 情報検索.
N2.n2-m8: Master formal conjunctions and logic markers (よって, ついては, 〜にして, 〜上での) — the cohesion toolkit of N2 texts — and read full argumentative essays.
N2.n2-m9: Turn knowledge into exam performance: skimming 長文, strategies for each N2 reading type (including 統合理解), and 50 minutes of single-play full-speed listening stamina.
N2.n2-m10: Take a complete N2 mock in Real mode, review mistakes by category and strand, and close remaining gaps before the real exam.

N1.n1-m1: Recognize classical forms (〜ぬ, 〜ず, 〜き, 〜けり) for reading recognition — not production — and master full である style and classical rhetoric (体言止め, 倒置, 係り結び) as the foundation for literary and formal texts.
N1.n1-m2: Master ultra-formal written keigo and complete business letters: 拝啓〜敬具 structure, 謹んで, 恐れながら, social formulas, and ご〜いただく & お〜申し上げる — as a life skill and exam material.
N1.n1-m3: Build formal written arguments with purpose, conformity, and basis patterns: 〜べく/〜べくも, 〜んがため(に), 〜と相まって, 〜に即して, 〜に則って, 〜を踏まえて — then write a full argumentative essay.
N1.n1-m4: Distinguish near-synonyms through minimal contrast (〜にかこつけて, 〜にかまけて, 〜をよそに, 〜ならいざしらず, 〜はさておき, 〜はおろか, 〜もさることながら) and read short 社説 with author-stance comprehension.
N1.n1-m5: Read authentic 社説 and opinion columns (〜たりとも, 〜だに, 〜とは比べものにならない, 〜を余儀なくされる/させる, 〜の至り/〜の極み), compare two opposing texts, and write an argued response.
N1.n1-m6: Read literary criticism and essays with assertiveness/futility patterns (〜てはばからない/〜を憚らない, 〜も顧みず/〜をものともせず, 〜甲斐もなく, 〜たが最後), recognize literary style (inversion, ellipsis), and write a review.
N1.n1-m7: Master advanced near-synonyms (〜ようでは, 〜ようによっては, 〜まい/〜ずじまい) and use 四字熟語 correctly — meaning, reading, register, context — in formal writing.
N1.n1-m8: Understand abstract fast-paced lectures and panel discussions (implied meaning, speaker stance, 統合理解) and master advanced onomatopoeia as a literary rhetorical device.
N1.n1-m9: Turn knowledge into exam performance: timed skimming of long authentic texts, 主張理解 & 情報検索 strategies, eliminating near-synonym distractors, and 60 minutes of single-play listening stamina.
N1.n1-m10: Take two full N1 mocks in Real mode (170 minutes), review mistakes by category and strand, close remaining gaps, and complete the N1 readiness checklist.
